title: Scientists read this ancient burnt scroll without unrolling it 🌋👀 #trendingshorts #ai #tech
description:
A global contest is paying out hundreds of thousands of dollars to anyone who can read scrolls that no human has been able to open for 2,000 years.

They're called the Herculaneum scrolls, and they were burned into solid charcoal when Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79, burying a luxury Roman villa and its entire library.

For centuries they were unreadable. Trying to physically unroll them caused the brittle layers to flake off and disintegrate.

So in 2023, researchers launched the Vesuvius Challenge, inviting teams to crack the problem with AI instead.

The technique scans a scroll with high-resolution X-rays, then trains machine learning to detect faint traces of ancient ink by spotting subtle differences in the fibers.

It built on a breakthrough by computer scientist Brent Seales, who first proved the hidden writing could be read without ever touching it.

Now one scroll has been virtually unwrapped, revealing 20 columns of text across more than a meter of charred papyrus.

It turned out to be a work on stoic philosophy, possibly written by an ancient Greek philosopher.

With the method proven, the race is now on to read hundreds more.
